newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's INA says to sell non-core assets in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's INA says to sell non-core assets in 1997.

text.p: Croatia's state-owned oil firm INA said on Thursday it would concentrate on its core business in 1997 in a bid to improve efficiency and pave the way for a foreign listing.
"In 1999, we plan to come to the London Stock Exchange and be sold worldwide," company chief executive Andrija Kojakovic told an investment conference.
"Next year we are planning to spin off all businesses except crude oil and gas production," he added.
Kojavic said loss-making plastic and fertiliser plants as well as INA's stakes in tourist firms would be sold outright or privatised in another way.
INA would try to reduce its workforce from the current 27,000 in an effort to cut costs while increasing investments in refineries and petrol stations in the next four years.
The company would invest heavily in expanding production to 4.0 billion from the current 1.7 billion tonnes of crude annually by year 2000.
INA also planned to establish itself on the markets of neighbouring countries, including Slovenia, Bosnia and Hungary.
"We want to hold the second or third place in those markets," Kojakovic said. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
